svg.text: Completion 21% (45 of 211 items implemented or verified) · Verified 0% (0) · Current milestone: M1 — Evidence
Generated from progress/progress.toml by tools/progress-gen. Completion = (implemented + verified) / total; floored.

rect.title: M0 — Foundation: Implemented — Stage A: workspace, hygiene, progress tooling, docs, Windows gate, CI and the source root all exist and work. RE applications are installed when first needed.

g.title: M1 — Evidence: Partial — Stage B: regulatory and official sources catalogued, official mobile software inventoried, formats identified.

M2 — Import: Partial — Stage C. Scanner, manifest, normalised layout and two importer stages (loose media, and media inside ZIP-family archives read within a budget) exist and are tested on synthetic files. No proprietary container is unpacked, and no real source material has been imported into an asset set.
M3 — Headless game model: Partial — Stage D: state, spin, awards, feature state machine, deterministic traces. Runs on a synthetic fixture only; original mathematics unknown.

M4 — Golden Century Bevy slice: Partial — The app plays Golden Century (synthetic maths) with the authentic art, animations and sound of the owner's mobile build from a local pack, in the cabinet frame the owner chose. Reels, wins, free games, Hold & Spin and its payout follow timings and sounds measured on the official app's recording (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_PRESENTATION.md). Not yet near-1:1 throughout: side-by-side comparison, unplaced sounds, attract mode and the hidden maths remain.

rect.title: M5 — Parity: Not started — Stage F: source-vs-rewrite traces, timing, screenshots, animation and audio events, discrepancies tracked.
M6 — Portability: Not started — Stage G: Windows verified, Linux and macOS build and test, Web/WASM builds and runs.
M8 — Game mathematics recovered and explained: Investigating — Parallel lane. Analysis tooling exists and is tested on the synthetic fixture; no original mathematics is held, and none is public.

g.title: M7 — The other seven titles: Partial — Scope widened to eight titles (D-018). Autumn Moon, Happy & Prosperous, Panda Magic, Genghis Khan, Golden Gong, Peace & Long Life and Spring Festival play in the cabinet from their own local packs, chosen from the machine menu, each with its own help-page pay table, symbols and free-games feature on Golden Century's engine and presentation. Maths synthetic; none compared side by side with its own footage yet.

rect.title: Foundation / Repository bootstrap (workspace, licence, toolchain pin) — Implemented
Foundation / Legal and project policy — Implemented
Foundation / Evidence labels and provenance rules — Implemented
Foundation / Private source root outside Git — Implemented

g.title: Foundation / Windows development environment (reproducible) — Partial — Rust, MSVC, wasm32, Git, Python, Java, ffmpeg, and the Android emulator with platform tools are installed and recorded in docs/BUILDING.md. Decompiler applications are installed as the analysis needs them.

rect.title: Foundation / Windows pre-merge gate — Implemented — All nine steps active: fmt, clippy, test, hygiene, progress, app build, smoke launch, wasm32 build, release build.
Foundation / CI (Linux, Windows, macOS, wasm32 check) — Implemented
Foundation / Repository hygiene checker — Implemented
Foundation / Progress tracker and generator — Implemented
Foundation / Prior-art review (ASAMU-decomp, rea, universal-modder) — Implemented

Reverse engineering / Dragon Link cabinet and platform research — Implemented — Generations, base-software lineage and the launch cabinets are documented from regulators' records and the manufacturer's archived pages. The internals of Gen8 and later are not public.

Reverse engineering / Regulatory source inventory — Implemented — ACT register swept 2016 to 2026; Victoria and one US regulator mined; the national standard's requirements recorded. No title-level register exists publicly for NSW, Qld, SA, Tas, NT or WA. No Australian return figure for Dragon Link exists publicly.

g.title: Reverse engineering / Official mobile reference inventory — Partial — Mighty Fu Casino 5.6.0 obtained from the Play Store, hashed and inventoried, with the content it downloaded for Golden Century (docs/reverse-engineering/MOBILE_PACKAGE.md). The downloaded packages of all four titles in scope, and of four further Dragon Link titles, are held.

rect.title: Reverse engineering / Source provenance database (claims) — Implemented

g.title: Reverse engineering / Package and file-format identification — Partial — Tools exist and have been run on a real package: Unity IL2CPP identified; two unfamiliar formats measured, a MERC container and an .enc family consistent with a block cipher. Neither is understood yet.

Reverse engineering / Executable analysis — Partial — The app's large native library is identified as the manufacturer's native game runtime (one pass). The IL2CPP side is unexamined. Analysis of the protection on the game tables was stopped (BLOCKERS B-005).

Reverse engineering / Asset-container identification — Partial — The MERC container is understood by a private parser that reads every such file of eight titles. A private exporter (outside Git) takes Golden Century's art, animation sequences and sound into a local, ignored pack the app loads; the repository's own importer does not do this yet.

Reverse engineering / Texture and image extraction — Partial — Golden Century's textures (raw RGBA and ETC1) and sprite cuts are decoded by the private exporter into the local pack. Not a committed tool.

rect.title: Reverse engineering / Font identification — Not started

g.title: Reverse engineering / Audio extraction — Partial — Golden Century's 114 Ogg clips, the seven sister titles' clips and the app's shared sound bank (three payout tracks) are carved by private tooling into the local pack. Not a committed tool.

Reverse engineering / Animation extraction — Partial — Golden Century's image sequences and alpha video animations are exported by private tooling to frame folders in the local pack. Not a committed tool.
Reverse engineering / Configuration and data extraction — Blocked

rect.title: Reverse engineering / Mathematical-model investigation — Investigating — No cabinet mathematics is held and none is public. The mobile build's tables are held but protected and unread (BLOCKERS B-005); it is established that the four titles are two pairs sharing their tables in that build. A public-sources pass is running.
Mathematics and analysis / Per-constant provenance model — Implemented

Mathematics and analysis / Machine-readable game configuration — Implemented — Exercised only on the synthetic fixture. Cannot yet express free games, feature reels, weighted stops or progressive meters.
Mathematics and analysis / Exact base-game analysis (line and scatter return, composition) — Implemented

Mathematics and analysis / Exact Hold & Spin analysis (trigger, outcome distribution, value, jackpot frequency) — Implemented — For the generic one-chance-per-position feature model; the original feature mechanics are unknown.
Mathematics and analysis / Hit frequency and base-game variance by enumeration — Implemented
Mathematics and analysis / Seeded Monte Carlo with confidence intervals — Implemented
Mathematics and analysis / Progressive jackpot expected-value calculator — Implemented — Assumes probabilities independent of the meters. No meter model yet.
Mathematics and analysis / Configuration and version comparison — Implemented
Mathematics and analysis / Per-game technical report generator — Implemented
Mathematics and analysis / Whole-spin volatility — Implemented — Exact when the stop combinations can be enumerated; otherwise simulated with the run stated.
Mathematics and analysis / Free-games mathematics — Not started
Mathematics and analysis / Progressive meter model (contribution, increments, resets) — Not started
Mathematics and analysis / Virtual-reel and weighted-stop representation — Not started — Every stop is equally likely in the current model.

Mathematics and analysis / Reel-strip reconstruction from observed windows — Implemented — Window shares with intervals, a test of equal stop likelihood, an estimate of unseen windows, and exact strip assembly with the number of equivalent orders. Exercised on our own simulation only; no observed game yet. Feature probabilities are not reconstructed.

g.title: Mathematics and analysis / Reel windows transcribed from public cabinet footage — Partial — Rung 1b (DECISIONS D-015). One 53-minute Australian session of Golden Century: 583 games, every one read, 1,808 reel windows read twice by different readers with no disagreement. At $1, two of five reels assemble as candidate strips (one fitting its counts well, one only just) now that the reconstruction finds windows that sit at more than one stop; three reels still miss windows, and no cent-denomination reel assembles. One session of one title; strips are kept privately.

rect.title: Mathematics and analysis / Automated spin collection from the official mobile app — Not started — Only relevant if observed spins become the route to the mobile build's mathematics. May meet the same limit as BLOCKERS B-005; not assumed available.
Mathematics and analysis / Statistical validation against captured gameplay — Not started

Mathematics and analysis / Recovered configuration: Golden Century — Investigating — No source held. An online evidence pass over litigation, regulatory, archival and research sources is under way (docs/BLOCKERS.md); it is not treated as blocked until those are exhausted.

Mathematics and analysis / Recovered configuration: Happy & Prosperous — Investigating — No source held. An online evidence pass over litigation, regulatory, archival and research sources is under way (docs/BLOCKERS.md); it is not treated as blocked until those are exhausted.

Mathematics and analysis / Recovered configuration: Panda Magic — Investigating — No source held. An online evidence pass over litigation, regulatory, archival and research sources is under way (docs/BLOCKERS.md); it is not treated as blocked until those are exhausted.

Mathematics and analysis / Recovered configuration: Autumn Moon — Investigating — No source held. An online evidence pass over litigation, regulatory, archival and research sources is under way (docs/BLOCKERS.md); it is not treated as blocked until those are exhausted.

g.title: Mathematics and analysis / Player-visible pay tables, lines and bet structures — Partial — US pay tables and Hold & Spin rules of three titles transcribed from machines' rules screens in public footage; Australian lines by denomination, fixed prize values and free-games awards read from play for all four. No pay table for Golden Century, no Australian rules screen, no full bet ladder and no return figure were found (docs/reverse-engineering/FOOTAGE.md).

rect.title: Mathematics and analysis / Denomination and bet effects — Investigating — First direct observation on an Australian Dragon Link machine: Golden Century at $1 shows different reel windows and one different pay from the 1c to 10c games, which are consistent with one configuration; changing lines does not change the reels (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_SESSION.md). Inferred statistically from one session. Lightning Link return by denomination and the regulatory limits are in PUBLISHED_RETURNS.md. No return figure for Dragon Link in Australia.

Mathematics and analysis / Mathematical differences between program versions — Investigating — Identifiers of every Australian generation and of US builds are recorded, and the manufacturer says dozens of iterations share a similar design (LITIGATION.md). What differs is not public.

Mathematics and analysis / RNG architecture and call sites — Investigating — Mobile: the generator family and the unbiased bounded draw are known from static analysis of the app (MOBILE_MATH_ARCHITECTURE.md); seeding is recorded privately and not published (DECISIONS D-016). Cabinet: regulatory requirements by revision are documented; the product's algorithm, seeding and call sites are not public.

Mathematics and analysis / Outcome selection, reel-stop relationship and input timing — Investigating — Mobile: the order of a round is known from static analysis: stops, prize-symbol values over the whole strip, window, evaluation, then features (MOBILE_MATH_ARCHITECTURE.md). Cabinet: regulation requires the outcome before presentation and forbids timing from changing the distribution; not verified in any cabinet software.

Mathematics and analysis / State dependence and persistence between spins — Investigating — Mobile: the state carried inside Hold & Spin is known (held symbols, count, one specially weighted position); no state carried between base games was found in the code examined, which is not proof of absence. Cabinet: regulation permits only declared tokens and progressive pools; not verified in software.

Mathematics and analysis / Mobile versus cabinet mathematics — Investigating — The mobile algorithms are described and their numbers unread; the cabinet has pay entries and reel windows from footage and no algorithm. They agree on what both show (Hold & Spin counts, the free-games reveal). The mobile engine can select reels by bet configuration, and a cabinet used different reels at $1: a resemblance. No table can be compared yet.

Mathematics and analysis / Progressive break-even thresholds of the originals — Investigating — No source held. An online evidence pass over litigation, regulatory, archival and research sources is under way (docs/BLOCKERS.md); it is not treated as blocked until those are exhausted.

Mathematics and analysis / Classification of player beliefs against evidence — Not started — Classes defined in docs/reverse-engineering/math/QUESTIONS.md; none can be judged without a recovered configuration.
Shared game runtime / Outcome source abstraction (test, record, replay) — Implemented — Test instruments of ours. Models nothing about the original generator, which is unknown.

g.title: Shared game runtime / State machine — Partial — Idle, free-games and Hold & Spin phases and the gamble, with transactional commands; no attract or idle states.

Shared game runtime / Credits / play-credit model — Partial — A play-credit meter with chained credit events. A denomination change recounts the credits so the money is unchanged, holding what does not make a whole credit (ChangeDenomination, tested). Cash handling (notes, tickets, collect) is not modelled.

rect.title: Shared game runtime / Bet selection — Implemented — Credits per line and line counts (SetBet, SetLines, SetStake). The cabinet build holds the presentation as data: club (default) with credits keys that select and lines keys that set the lines and play, per-denomination ladders from footage; casino with fixed lines and bet keys that play (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_CABINET_DECK.md). The credits row at 5c and 10c is not legible on footage.

g.title: Shared game runtime / Spin lifecycle — Partial — Bet, reel stops, awards, feature entry, completion as events; ordering is ours, not evidenced.
Shared game runtime / Reel model — Partial — Strips with a wrapping window; how the original maps outcomes to stops is unknown.
Shared game runtime / Symbol model — Partial — Regular, wild, scatter and orb kinds; title symbol sets are unknown.
Shared game runtime / Pay evaluator — Partial — Generic left-to-right line rules and scatter pays, each stated in eval.rs; none checked against the original.

rect.title: Shared game runtime / Win presentation — Implemented — Win tunes chosen by the win's size where measured, counts lasting the tune's audible length, lines in turn with their symbols blinking (the club cabinet's two even 0.66 s cycles a line, STRONG), symbol animations, a coin shower for big wins.

g.title: Shared game runtime / Feature triggering — Partial — Hold & Spin by orb count, free games by scatter count; a spin that wins both plays Hold & Spin first and then the free games, completing (and offering the gamble) only after both (the owner). The trigger counts are evidenced; the chances are synthetic.
Shared game runtime / Hold & Spin framework — Partial — Parameterised respin loop with tests; trigger count, respins, chances and values are synthetic.

Shared game runtime / Jackpot model and presentation — Partial — Four tiers on a jackpot bar, awarded in Hold & Spin (full grid awards the Grand). Golden Century: Mini and Minor fixed by denomination as club footage shows them (1,000 / 5,000 credits to 10c, 250 / 1,250 at $1); Major and Grand progressive meters the core pays and restarts, climbing a cent or two every few seconds in the app with rolling figures; the Grand restarts at $10,000 as filmed. Meter openings, exact rates, the Major's restart and the ceilings are synthetic; odds unknown.

rect.title: Shared game runtime / Free-game framework — Implemented — Scatter trigger, an award of free games on their own reels played without a bet, a mystery-symbol reveal (one drawn symbol fills every mystery position), retrigger, and a clean return to the base game. Modelled as FreeGamesModel; the synthetic Golden Century config uses it. The exact free-game strips, reveal weights and retrigger size are synthetic.

Shared game runtime / Audio — Implemented — Plays clips from the local pack: one-shots, loops, cues scheduled to the presentation, a fade. Placements follow recordings (GOLDEN_CENTURY_PRESENTATION.md).
Shared game runtime / Animation — Implemented — Reels at the measured speed, cadence and landing; respin positions as the real game's; feature sequences on measured timings.

Shared game runtime / VFX — Implemented — The game's own animation sequences: symbol win animations, tall wilds, door reveal, fire rings, bursts, fire transitions, collection comets, coin shower and banner bursts.

Shared game runtime / UI — Implemented — The cabinet screen with the jackpot bar, CREDIT/BET/WIN meters (the club's dollars and credits alternation in PLAY ON, the gamble and after a denomination choice), the club's system messages (gamble notice, win limit, cash-in notice, a stand-in greeting), N LINES boxes, the GAMES MENU denomination chooser and the gamble screen; the Australian club deck as filmed (GAMBLE over TAKE WIN, credits and lines keys, all lit, the selected lines key light blue; the teardrop pointing up, dark but for START FEATURE, with PLAY/REPEAT BET/START FEATURE/SPIN; GOOD LUCK wiping in and out on every spin and respin, CHOOSE; the 1 Hz flash; the gamble's lattice keys), or the casino style; a four-title launcher. Not compared side by side throughout (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_CABINET_DECK.md).

Shared game runtime / Input — Implemented — Deck keys and touch-screen tabs by pointer, and the keyboard: credits and lines keys (club) or bet keys (casino), PLAY, the GAMES MENU with its confirmation, gamble choices on keys and screen, half gamble, take win; a spin is refused until the reels are still. No autoplay or settings menu yet.

g.title: Shared game runtime / Save and settings handling — Partial — Game state serialises and resumes mid-feature; no settings, no persistence in an app.

rect.title: Golden Century / Title identity, versions and regulatory identifiers — Implemented — ACT specifications across generations, Victorian builds, US personality identifiers and the 2016 Australian launch are recorded. NSW and Queensland approvals are not public; what changed between generations is unknown.

g.title: Golden Century / Reel layout and lines — Partial — Five by three. Club machines: lines chosen on the deck, 1/5/10/30/50 at 1c and 2c, 1/5/10/20/25 at 10c, 1 to 5 at $1. Casino style: lines fixed (50 at The Star; 50/50/25/5 by denomination on a US machine). The shapes of lines 1 to 5 established from win messages; lines 6 to 50 not found.

Golden Century / Symbol set — Partial — Symbol set described from Australian play in public footage; roles of scatter, wild, prize symbol and mystery symbol observed. No rules text found, so the set may be incomplete. No artwork held.

Golden Century / Paytable — Partial — Sixteen pay-table entries read from win messages in one transcribed Australian session, one of them differing between $1 and the cent denominations, and checked against a separate reading of the credit meter: 221 of 221 $1 games paid exactly what they give (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_SESSION.md). Incomplete; no rules screen found.

Golden Century / Denominations and bet options — Partial — Two presentations read from footage: Australian club machines (1c-$1 on a chooser asking ARE YOU SURE?, credits keys that select and lines keys that play, ladders per denomination) and a casino style (Bet Multiplier, fixed lines, bet keys that play) seen at The Star and, mostly, on a US machine. The credits row at 5c and 10c and any Australian casino deck are not legible (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_CABINET_DECK.md).

rect.title: Golden Century / Reel strips and weighting — Not started

g.title: Golden Century / Hold & Spin rules and presentation — Partial — Presentation follows the official app recording step by step (trigger, respins, counter, payout and its music) and club cabinet footage where it differs: one fire into the board with no medallion, PRESS START FEATURE BUTTON blinking, the first respin 0.59 s after the count, a blue-white flash on the 3, thin pale row lines, the cabinet's status line, every tally on a WINNER box over the jackpot bar at the cabinet's pace, a white banner amount (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_PRESENTATION.md). Rules, values and weights are synthetic.

Golden Century / Jackpot levels and presentation — Partial — Australia, from public footage: Grand and Major are running meters; Mini and Minor are fixed per denomination (1,000 and 5,000 credits up to 10c; 250 and 1,250 at $1). Strong evidence the Grand is linked and the Major stand-alone. Start-up values, rates and ceilings not public. Implemented: the Mini and Minor footage values by denomination; Major and Grand meters the core pays and restarts and the app climbs at the club machines' order of rate, rolling changed figures as filmed, the Grand restarting at $10,000 as filmed; each jackpot's chance the stake over its prize, so the return is about 90% at every bet (the national standard's rule); through Hold & Spin the cabinet's COLLECTED disc with the corner jackpots, a Major first on its own plaque, the Grand under the fire with its status and attendant lines. The meters' openings, exact rates, the Major's restart and the ceilings, the chances and the odds are synthetic; presentation not compared side by side.

Golden Century / Free games feature — Partial — Three scatters award six free games; mystery doors reveal one symbol, the emperor and the coin among them (help screen); revealed coins carry prizes and six or more start Hold & Spin inside the free games, which then carry on (cabinet footage, STRONG); retriggers add three (owner). Presentation follows the official app recording (trigger sequence, a win's pace) and club cabinet footage where it differs (the trigger's status and message rows, the prompt with the scatter count, the 0.52 s start, the counter from 1 OF 0, the doors 0.30 s after the rest with the wins at + 1.5 s and a no-win game's next spin at + 2.0 s, the WIN banner only for big wins with a 10x limit that is HYPOTHESIS, the resume after a Hold & Spin inside, FEATURE COMPLETED after the last count with CREDIT held: y8c8lEdPW8Y, 1bAevGz0K2k). Strips and weights are synthetic.

Golden Century / Title artwork, UI layout and typography — Partial — The app renders Golden Century with the authentic art, animations and sound of the owner's mobile build from a local, ignored pack (never committed), in the cabinet frame the owner chose. Gameplay presentation follows the official app recording; not compared side by side throughout.

rect.title: Golden Century / Sound and music — Implemented — Each sound the app plays is a game clip placed where recordings show it (waveform-matched); placements not evidenced stay silent. Every unplaced clip was searched for in the footage and the scene files; those without a shown placement stay unplaced (GOLDEN_CENTURY_PRESENTATION.md).

Golden Century / Animation and sequence timing — Implemented — Reels spin and land as 60 fps cabinet footage shows (20 symbols a second, reels 0.45 s apart, through the stop to 0.65, back to 0.40, an 8-frame slide), measured on a muted capture of the app; results, free games, Hold & Spin and its payout follow timings measured frame by frame on the official app.

Golden Century / Attract / idle mode — Implemented — At zero credit the GAMES MENU opens after 30 s idle (HYPOTHESIS: the framework default); its top-screen PLAY plaque steps through the denominations with their Minor and Mini as club footage shows (VERIFIED timing), fire round the boxes. Not compared side by side throughout.

g.title: Golden Century / Locally imported original assets — Partial — Golden Century's art, animation and sound from the owner's mobile build are exported by private tooling into a local, ignored pack the app loads (DRAGONLINK_ART). The repository's importer and manifest do not produce it yet.

rect.title: Golden Century / Evidence-backed parity — Not started

Happy & Prosperous / Title identity, versions and regulatory identifiers — Implemented — ACT specifications across generations, Victorian builds, US personality identifiers and the 2016 Australian launch are recorded. NSW and Queensland approvals are not public; what changed between generations is unknown.

g.title: Happy & Prosperous / Reel layout and lines — Partial — Australia (Queensland clubs): five by three, with 50 lines at 1c and 2c, 25 at 5c and 10c, 5 at $1, read from public footage and the manufacturer's archived pages. Payline shapes and casino configurations incomplete.
Happy & Prosperous / Symbol set — Partial — Symbol set and roles read from US rules screens and Australian play in public footage; described, no artwork held.

Happy & Prosperous / Paytable — Partial — The US pay table is transcribed from the machine's own rules screens in public footage, and is the one quoted in the manufacturer's complaint (docs/reverse-engineering/FOOTAGE.md). Two Australian observations agree with it; the Australian pay-table screen itself has not been found.
Happy & Prosperous / Denominations and bet options — Partial — Australian denominations per state are established from the manufacturer's archived pages. The bet ladder is not found.

rect.title: Happy & Prosperous / Reel strips and weighting — Not started

g.title: Happy & Prosperous / Hold & Spin rules and presentation — Partial — Played to Golden Century's rules and presentation, which the mobile build shares with this title; values and weights synthetic.

Happy & Prosperous / Jackpot levels and presentation — Partial — As Golden Century's: Mini and Minor fixed by denomination, Major and Grand progressive meters climbing in the app; chances follow the stake; start values, rates and odds synthetic.

Happy & Prosperous / Free games feature — Partial — Six free games on royal-free reels (rebuilt, synthetic), three more on a retrigger (mobile and club footage), no mystery symbol; coins start Hold & Spin inside the free games.

Happy & Prosperous / Title artwork, UI layout and typography — Partial — Plays in the cabinet from its own local pack through the shared presentation (single-cell wild, no tall stack); not compared side by side with its footage.
Happy & Prosperous / Sound and music — Partial — The pack's own clips play where Golden Century's do; not checked title by title against recordings.

rect.title: Happy & Prosperous / Animation and sequence timing — Not started
Happy & Prosperous / Attract and idle presentation — Not started

g.title: Happy & Prosperous / Locally imported original assets — Partial — Art, animation and sound exported by the private exporter into a local pack; never in Git.

g.title: Autumn Moon / Reel layout and lines — Partial — Australia (Queensland clubs): five by three, with 50 lines at 1c and 2c, 25 at 5c and 10c, 5 at $1, read from public footage and the manufacturer's archived pages. Payline shapes and casino configurations incomplete.
Autumn Moon / Symbol set — Partial — Symbol set and roles read from US rules screens and Australian play in public footage; described, no artwork held.

Autumn Moon / Paytable — Partial — Australian club wins fit the mobile build's pay table and not the US one (claims/autumn-moon.toml paytable.au-club, STRONG); the model pays that table. The club pay-table screen itself has not been found.
Autumn Moon / Denominations and bet options — Partial — Australian denominations per state are established from the manufacturer's archived pages. The bet ladder is not found.

rect.title: Autumn Moon / Reel strips and weighting — Not started

g.title: Autumn Moon / Hold & Spin rules and presentation — Partial — Played to Golden Century's rules and presentation, which the mobile build gives Autumn Moon byte for byte; values and weights synthetic.

Autumn Moon / Jackpot levels and presentation — Partial — As Golden Century's: Mini and Minor fixed by denomination (family club footage), Major and Grand progressive meters climbing in the app; chances follow the stake; start values, rates and odds synthetic.

Autumn Moon / Free games feature — Partial — Six free games; the medallions open onto one symbol, the woman and the coin among them, coins starting Hold & Spin inside the free games; a retrigger adds six (three club recordings). Strips and weights synthetic.

Autumn Moon / Title artwork, UI layout and typography — Partial — Plays in the cabinet from its own local pack (exported privately from the mobile build), through the same presentation as Golden Century; not compared side by side with Autumn Moon footage.

Autumn Moon / Sound and music — Partial — The pack's own clips play where Golden Century's do; the club cabinet's free-games music matches the mobile one on one recording. Placements not checked title by title.

g.title: Genghis Khan / Title identity, versions and regulatory identifiers — Partial — ACT and US listings recorded in the private notes; Australian approvals not public.

Genghis Khan / Reel layout and lines — Partial — Five by three, fifty fixed-pattern lines read from the help page (VERIFIED, mobile); club decks sell lines per denomination (footage). That the cabinet uses the same fifty is HYPOTHESIS.
Genghis Khan / Symbol set — Partial — Woman, fortress, pot, shield, royals, the archer scatter, Khan the wild on reels 2-5, the coin (help pages, VERIFIED).

Genghis Khan / Paytable — Partial — The help page's table (woman 150/50/10/2, fortress 100/30/5, pot and shield 100/25/5, K 75/20/5, Q-9 50/10/5; archer 100/15/2 x bet; the wild pays nothing); three cabinet line wins agree (STRONG).

Parity / Behavioural trace format — Implemented — One JSON Lines format for rewrite traces and transcribed observations; headers that would mislead are refused. No observation trace exists yet.

g.title: Parity / Source recordings of the original — Partial — Public cabinet recordings of all four titles held privately with hashes; one Australian Golden Century session transcribed. The owner's own recording of the official mobile app (3:41 with sound, six excerpts) is the gameplay presentation reference. No recording is tied to a regulatory build.

rect.title: Parity / Recording to observation trace — Implemented — Rest moments are found in a recording and a still cut for each; a sheet of transcribed windows becomes an observation trace of one configuration, with nothing filled in and the meters checked against each other. The detector was run on one hand-held recording of a cabinet (583 games in 53 minutes). Reading the stills is not automated.

Parity / Event comparison — Implemented — Event-by-event comparison that states what kind of comparison it is. Exercised on rewrite traces and on a rewrite relabelled as an observation; never on a real observation.

Parity / Replay of observed outcomes — Implemented — The outcomes a trace shows are scripted through the simulation, so that what still differs is a difference in rules and not in luck; hidden choices and impossible observations are reported. Tested on rewrite traces relabelled as observations only: no observation of an original exists, and through the synthetic fixture a replay tests this machinery and nothing else.

g.title: Parity / Timing comparison — Partial — Timings in the official app recording are measured frame by frame and the app's timed runs compared with them by hand (docs/reverse-engineering/GOLDEN_CENTURY_PRESENTATION.md); no automated trace comparison yet.
Parity / Visual comparison — Partial — Frames of the app's unattended runs are captured and compared with recording frames by eye; no automated comparison.

Parity / Audio comparison — Partial — Sounds in recordings are identified by waveform cross-correlation with the game's clips, with control windows (private tooling); not yet automated against the app's output.

rect.title: Parity / Deterministic replay — Implemented — A recorded game of ours replays event for event from its draw log. This is determinism of our code, not parity.
Parity / Evidence-backed parity tests — Not started

g.title: Platforms / Windows — Partial — The app builds in debug and release and smoke-launches on the Windows host; the gate passes. Placeholder mode only.
Platforms / Linux — Partial — Headless crates and tools build and test in CI; no app yet.
Platforms / macOS — Partial — Headless crates and tools build and test in CI; no app yet.

Platforms / Web / WASM — Partial — The app is bundled for the browser by tools/dev/web.ps1 and checked in headless Edge: it starts, draws the placeholder banner, and a key press spins. Checked on the Windows host only; the bundle is 41 MB and is not optimised or hosted. Placeholder mode only.

Packaging / Source importer — Partial — Stages 1 and 2: standard media found loose, or as entries of ZIP-family archives, is taken into the asset set unchanged with its provenance and hashes; archive entries only when their size and CRC-32 verify, within a decompression budget. Dry-run on a held package read fourteen archives with no entry failing. No proprietary container is unpacked, nothing is converted, and nothing is identified as a particular asset.

rect.title: Packaging / Asset manifest — Implemented — Logical id, source package and path, both hashes, media type, title, category, provenance class, confidence, method. Verified against files; exercised with synthetic files only.

g.title: Packaging / Local full-package workflow — Partial — dragonlink-pack verifies an asset set and assembles executable, assets and a do-not-distribute notice outside any Git tree. Exercised end to end with synthetic files; the application cannot display imported assets yet.
Packaging / Public asset-free build — Partial — The app runs with no assets in a clearly labelled placeholder mode. No packaged release yet.
